reviews.text: [h1]Please follow this game but don't buy yet[/h1] I’ve been [b]enjoying my time[/b] with this game so far, but despite all its potential and strengths, [b]I can’t recommend it in its current state[/b]. There are simply too many rough edges holding it back. That said, I’m keeping it and [b]will be waiting for future updates[/b] because I truly believe this game [b]can become something great![/b] [h1]The Cons:[/h1] - For its price, the game doesn’t deliver enough content. I’ve spent around 3 hours, and I feel like I’ve already seen everything the current gameplay has to offer. - The AI is still very lacking. - Town building is extremely limited, you can’t place gates in walls, can’t choose where farms go, and uneven terrain makes building feel more like a burden than a strategic choice. - Units, spells, and buildings have far too few upgrades. - You can’t really build themed runs since the upgrade system is too restrictive. - The pet is cute but underdeveloped. It lacks interactions and upgrades, having evolution stages or intermediate forms would make it so much better. - The first mode doesn’t give enough time to properly build a city. - The second mode feels bugged or unclear (dungeons don’t start attacks if you lower the danger level). - The rats are more dangerous than the dungeons, this really needs balancing. - Speaking of danger, the challenge isn’t there. The lack of proper AI and useful fortifications means you have little control over town damage, while monsters are so weak that even at higher levels there’s no real threat. - The UI needs more work, especially the mini-map after expanding territory in unlimited mode. [h1]The Pros:[/h1] - I love the graphic design. - The game has enormous potential, the core gameplay loop is fun despite the flaws, and with more polish, it could be fantastic. - The pet, while underdeveloped, actually feels helpful, more so than in many other god games. - NPC diversity is great and lays the foundation for varied gameplay, as do the spells (though both need deeper upgrades and interactions). - The core concept is fresh and works as a great introduction to god games. - The tutorial is clear and easy to follow (though maybe because the game lacks complexity right now). - I love watching my town grow, adding difficulty sliders could make this experience more customizable for different playstyles.

《钱钱向前冲》是一款建设城镇的即时战略类游戏，在游戏中，我们将需要在一片怪物遍地的土地上建立起自己的城市，由于冒险者逐利，因此我们需要用金钱来吸引冒险者入驻城市，从最初的一个城堡几个建设工建起一座座城市，并向周边扩展，消灭敌人的哨塔，在夜晚抵御敌人的进攻！ 目前游戏内有两种模式，分别是7天守城和无尽模式，两个模式字如其意，倒没什么好说的，游戏的设定挺有趣，在城市里的人不是白白为我们打工的，我们需要给他们钱发布委托和命令，才可以让他们去完成探索、战斗、赚钱等任务，在夜幕降临时还可以委托他们守护城镇。 完成游戏任务内的任务，会掉落类似肉鸽的选Buff环节，会随机掉落建筑物图纸、主神技能等选项，提升建筑等级，也可以选择类似Buff提升属性，似乎不能重复刷取，不过个别诸如图书馆等特殊建筑可以重复建造升级不同选项，玩起来挺烧脑的。 相信不少人都是被这个画风给吸引到的，毕竟在看不太懂玩法的情况下，美术算是第一个门槛了，本作的美术确实不错，不管是怪物，还是角色的立绘都不错，很可爱的画风，建筑也很有意思，那个锻造所竟然是一个龙在喷火，可惜敌人来它不会攻击。 七天模式打通关了，这里说一下我的看法，初玩很惊艳，觉得这种画风真有意思，但是玩一会就会腻了，游戏性有点差，而且玩到后期怪堆的多了会卡，建筑太多了，也不方便管理，定委托虽然可以修改金钱，但感觉完全没有那个必要，不过如果喜欢城市建造类游戏还是可以试试的，因为有其亮点。 [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

Breast milk (sometimes spelled as breastmilk) or mother's milk is milk produced by the mammary glands in the breasts of women. Breast milk is the primary source of nutrition for newborn infants, comprising fats, proteins, carbohydrates, and a varying composition of minerals and vitamins. Breast milk also contains substances that help protect an infant against infection and inflammation, such as symbiotic bacteria and other microorganisms and immunoglobulin A, whilst also contributing to the healthy development of the infant's immune system and gut microbiome.

Worth waiting for a good while for it to iron our its flaws before playing. I can't recommend it at this stage. While its got good bones, and a lovely artstyle, it suffers from a lack of polish on the basics. Like builders choosing to constantly try to repair far off farms that are actively under attack rather than building the buildings they were asked to long before the farm got attacked. Enemies wander in constantly during the day from many directions so you constantly have issues of builders being scared away from building at the very start of the game because they don't flee if attacked, they flee if an enemy is in a frankly too large radius around them, so if a single enemy wanders over, until your starting unit kills it your builders just can't do anything for you and you waste time. Ironically the night when the attack waves start proves the most productive for builders because there enemies are concentrated in an area you can focus on defending rather than being on all sides. A small tangent but sometimes the fleeing AI of farmers and such will make them run for shelter directly through a monster and get them stuck for a time on the monster who is actively murdering them. Plus heroes will fight battles to the death which means if one wanders into a fight, especially early on when you have limited numbers, and manages to drag too many enemies to them. They'll die, wasting your money, and likely risking those enemies wandering over to your castle too. The castle itself has no basic defence and since heroes aren't controlled but directed by quests, you can't rely on them to defend it if something wanders in and starts gnawing on the castle, so building an archer tower is a necessity. This again also raises the issue of the builders and tax collectors fear. If they are at your castle, then they will be unable to leave if a single monster is outside crippling your economy. The game's wandering enemies require very hands on responses but the game's control scheme and systems are designed for being very hands off.

So... if you can get it on like 75% off, it would be worth it, but anymore and it isn't. EDIT 3: Okay, so, I've beaten a run of the first mode, killed the final boss. My opinion hasn't changed, but they seemed to have removed the random debt bombs, which is both nice but didn't need to be removed-just readjusted and balanced to be a reasonable additional hurdle on occasion. I also survived in a survival world-or whatever it's called-for 31 days before it was getting too laggy and far, far, too boring. I still say this game is only worth it at 50-75% off currently due to the present issues and sheer lack of content, but... I don't QUITE think I wasted my money any longer. I squeezed this stone and did, in fact, get some blood. Some of it was my own, but... as long as the devs put the time in, take feedback, add more content, the current state of the game is a good BASE for a more developed, better, actual game. Keep an eye on it if it looks interesting, but I still say your money is better spent elsewhere unless you want to throw the money at them to support and encourage the potential that exists below the shiny, but empty, surface. EDIT 2: HOLY... She-hit. I just ACCIDENTALLY pushed the "N" button and found a menu that lets me control tax rates and shows me my projected income... this is so valuable and important, but the game has never even REMOTELY hinted something like this exists in the game. THAT, is a prime example of what I'm talking about with how this game tells you nothing. Not even a CORE mechanic was made clear to even exist... it took and accidental missed "B" click to find it. WOW. Over 20 hours of playtime... EDIT UPDATE: I'm stubborn with wasted money on games and tend to keep pushing through for as long as I can. Thing is, I don't think this is a well realized vision, but I don't writhe in agony the entire time playing. It's awfully frustrating at point, but never overwhelmingly so. A game SHOULDN'T be frustrating most of the time though. That said, this update is to say that I've run into a few bugs, one where my Godbeast died and had NEGATIVE time remaining before coming back, so the time just kept doing down further into negative and she was never going to wake up, almost lost a tile due to that. Also, there is a memory leak of some sort. The game hit over 6GB of RAM usage... this game SHOULD NOT demand even half that with how it looks and what's going on in it. It then frozen, showed me menus I've never seen before, then I had to force shut it down. I had another time where I also had like 9 FPS suddenly, and it only cleared up once I finished the tile, so something was going wrong somewhere in that map... Oh, another new addition that is happening now is that if I click on my Godbeast, the game freezes and I have to force close it. This game feels like it was half thought through, then half of that was actually finished. It looks great, the art is wonderful-but that's just about where most of the redeeming qualities stop. The tutorial... exists? It does make you aware of stuff... but doesn't really explain much. Very little information is given in-game anywhere. You'll find yourself looking at something and wondering how it actually functions, what it's actually accomplishing, what upgrades actually do, and plenty more. The economy part of this is absolutely terrible and poorly thought out, I think they wanted to do something a bit different but... it's just a nightmare to understand. You'll get the basics of it fine, that's the weird part, at first glance it you won't notice that the economy is actually eldritch mind-torture... but then you'll just get lost, again, because no information is given. It legitimately seems like the devs have never played a videogame in their lives, EVERYTHING that is wrong with this game is something that anyone that has played games in their life would have known to do better on-because you would remember all the times you've had those, "I wish this or that about this mechanic or that tooltip description." It's like they learned how to make a game with great art, without actually knowing anything about games? There is SOME enjoyment here, but it's scarce, running dry when you realize that about 1 hour in you might have seen everything the game has to offer? The main gameplay loops is flawed at the core. You spend a bunch of time building up a town, doing specific quests, and then if you win (unlikely), you lose all your progress and get to start from scratch with new objective. The scaling of the difficulty also doesn't care and you may be stuck picking between a soul crushingly challenging tile or a tile that will give you testicular torsion in real life (you'll even feel the pain if you wouldn't normally be equipped for it, ladies). It's not a fun challenging either. It's just bad. Just plain, simple, bad. I don't know what they were thinking, but this game needs another full year of careful, directed, development after the devs have played a handful of other games in the genre and similar genres so they know what a game is supposed to feel and play like. Maybe pay less for art and more for. mechanics, tooltips with accurate and informational descriptions... common sense and genre savviness? It's rough. Very rough. I wanted to love it, but now I'm just thoroughly disappointed I can't refund it. It just takes too long to get to the point where your realize there is nothing in there to salvage the experience.

I really like the game. The heroes, the combinations between different heroes, and the art are all 10/10. But in its current state, it is completely pointless to play. The balance is broken. You need perfect spawn, you cannot make a single mistake during the whole game, and you basically need perfect prediction of what is going to happen next. Even after all that, your units can still kill each other during training or end up on low health before a boss wave. And if you somehow survive all of that, you then have to pay a random tax to maintain your units, where the cost can be all the money you collected during the entire day. The tax system should be completely abolished if the game is supposed to have any real sense of progression. There is absolutely no way to recover from mistakes. Any damage to your base is basically game over, because everything is so expensive that spending money on repairs or buying new heroes slowly kills your run anyway.

I gave this game a do not recommend after about 5 hours of play, and now I am changing it to a recommend, with a few BIG caveats. First, this game is complex, counterintuitive and hard. Arguably way too hard. There's a ton to learn and it's easy to fail. Expect to restart constantly as your understanding grows, because the systems are extremely deep and largely hidden. The current tutorial and tooltips are inadequate, but this is also just the kind of game where there's a lot of trial and error involved. Second, the UI is not good. It's really easy to miss important functions. Lastly, the performance is pretty bad, and the game is pretty buggy. This makes the game's endless mode unplayable past a certain point, even cranking down the settings until my screen is just pixel vomit. But, I can't NOT recommend this game after playing it for like 6 hours straight tonight. If the idea of a god game made by Nippon Ichi sounds appealing to you, that's basically what you're getting. Every single thing about the game is charming the way a NIS game is. And once you do understand the game loop, it's insanely addictive and fun. I think if you can stomach a brickwall learning curve and some jank, there's a really unique game here.

I absolutely loved the game's concept, visuals, and attention to the music. But I swear, I just couldn’t fully grasp it. I tried playing Conquest mode, and by the end of the first day it felt like the entire army of Mordor showed up at my doorstep. And it wasn’t just a failure — I got completely crushed to the point where I genuinely have no idea what I could have done differently or what I did so wrong. The game really needs a much better tutorial. I didn’t understand anything about synergies, I couldn’t find the passives for each character, I didn’t know what each unit was actually good at, and I couldn’t tell how much money each building was generating. In short: I was extremely lost. Like, REALLY lost. I’m not asking for a refund because I truly believe this game can become incredible. It just needs polish. And honestly, I think one of the magic words missing right now is predictability — not in gameplay or events, but in information clarity. For example: showing the strength of the next horde, explaining why a level 2 hero survived a dungeon while a level 7 hero died on the first room, or giving more transparent feedback in general. Not predictability in outcomes, but predictability in understanding: what each thing does, why it does it, and how it works. If this same game becomes more polished in the future, I genuinely believe it has the potential to become one of my favorite games. For now, I’m leaving a negative review not because the game is necessarily bad, but because I’ll be eagerly following every new version, hoping to eventually turn this into a VERY positive review.

《钱钱向钱冲》是一款画风非常治愈的融合了即时战略要素的建造游戏，不过可能和大家常玩的即时战略游戏有点不同，本作加入了模拟经营要素和冒险探索内容，而且在编队方向是也有些独特，并不是由我们进行特定分组的编队，而是通过发布任务的方式着急人手。总体来说上手稍微有点门槛，还存在一些指令优先级冲突的情况。 游戏玩法比较容易理解，开局玩家只有城堡和神兽，每种神兽的特色buff是不同的。然后玩家要利用初始卡牌建造东西，不过这个初始是带有类似肉鸽要素的随机性质的，一般来说初始都是建军营，然后招募一些冒险者。 这里面的冒险者风格其实有点类似“开罗游戏”的模式，那就是他们有自己的收入来源，所以他们要在我们这个小镇上消费，我们才能赚钱，我们赚钱了才能给他们发布悬赏让他们干活，再给他们分钱，这样就会形成一条明晰的正向循环线路。 探索部分本应是游戏比较自由的部分，不过我们只能通过悬赏进行一定程度的吸引，有时候不知道为什么有些冒险者不会前去，有点像自走棋的感觉，但是因为这是个大地图游戏，所以自走棋判定的范围更大，也更容易丢失目标。在迷宫里也可以设置副本奖励和BOSS的位置，这个设计还挺巧妙的。总体来说一个是刷装备，另一个就是提升等级。因为没到晚上都会有敌人对我们的建筑进行攻击，城堡被攻破了就是游戏结束了，其余的建筑破了对我们的资金来说一笔不下的损失。所以提升冒险者等级是非常有必要的。 经营系统也比较一般，游戏里的资源种类很少，建筑建成之后收钱的方式还非常麻烦，风格倒不是硬核，只是单纯的繁琐。游戏最大的特点那就是画面美术没得说，很可爱很治愈。 不足之处 1、优先级好像有点问题，有时候发布悬赏总有人叫不来。 2、玩法比较固定，虽然有点肉鸽要素，但对游戏的重复性体验帮助不大 3、新手教程有点不够明，建议再简单一些。 4、内容量不足 总结 个人感觉，《钱钱向钱冲》是一款靠美术提了不少分的即时战略游戏，主要各个方面都比较浅显，而且怪物的等级提升的都很快，所以我们的培养注定要走特定的反向，限制了这类游戏的发展。目前而言，游戏基本玩法不错，但内容偏少，希望日后能多更新一些内容，让游戏玩法变得更加丰富。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

I hope this game gets a sequel, but I can't recommend this. It's inspired, it's a cool concept, but it tries to wear 10 hats all at once and it didn't really feel like it ever came together. Just under 4 hours in and unfortunately I think I've have my fill, and feel like I'm wasting my time. My main issue is there is alot happening but simultaneously nothing happening. Town management, hero questing, dungeon exploring, pet care. Town production and sales are done passively/Questing, looting and hero leveling are completed passively/dungeon exploring is done passively you have a combat log but there's not really any indication of outcomes or victories/Parties are formed passively/pet care, exists? there's a "behaviour reinforcement" aspect but I never felt the need to engage with it. A lot of this feels as though it stems from everything happening at the same thing and the game might've benefited from a more reeled in scope and more defined sections. Because there is so little player interaction as well, a lot of the games' systems can feel as though they exist within an echo chamber even though they do have passive cross interaction. Quickly getting over the rest of it: Performance - The animation system is apparently locked to single core and it shows. There's a constant 40 fps to enjoy from bottlenecking and you'll find it even in the earliest of missions. UI Sizing - Dungeons are so passive you don't need to read this menus, but regardless they're tiny. There are scale options but they affect the whole UI, which means blocking your screen to get dungeon UI readable. Upgrades - There's very surface level specializations and randomness of perks doesn't really allow you to try and tailor towns. Hero upgrades are done automatically, they passively loot/buy/sell/craft equipment Lack of info - Was the dungeon a success? How/When did I get a corrupt mooladin? What's generating me money? What are my resources like? How powerful are my heroes? The game doesn't convey much to you, you'll get stuff, complete stuff, level heroes these are objectives of your town management but they just kind of happen in the back ground Camera - It's at an awkward angle, your towns will be an unreadable clump (not helped by the fact you need to clump buildings together to get synergies). combat will happen in stacks of trees. It's lucky there's so little to actively do or it'd be a much bigger hinderance. Building - Buildings have arbitrary feeling zones around which they block the building of other buildings beyond that of the and you must terraform level ground for them to be built. They leads to town building feeling clunky Buildings' Menus - There are so many buildings with "Enter" options or menu pop ups that have no need for them. It's just unneccessary. Yandere - It's so weirdly out of place. It's the one unit in the game that requires you to baby sit them with a meta mechanic for whatever reason (not even your God/Pet character has any active maintenance). If you don't you'll get meta interactions or they'll attack villagers/turn into a boss. They will also get mad if you don't give them attention while in dungeons. I also can't stress that this is the only unit with any sort of interaction/management in the game. There's no pay off to following the mechanics either, it's not particularly difficult just a chore, and unless you roll a sacrafice spell you're also stuck with them. Little Town Management - You don't have control of what the marketplace is stocked with, you don't have control over what equipment is made, you don't have control over what parties are formed. You set farm bounties, and taxes. Questing - The whole gimmick the game is built around, is boiled down to "Attach a cost to a move command and maybe it's enough to entice the AI". Music - It's good but there's just not a lot. You will hear the same song over and over. The issue is since there's lyrics as well it's hard not to notice either. Variety - I never really felt like I had to change my style of play to meet objectives. I built stuff, the game played itself and eventually you win. Overall you don't really have an active role and the game largely feels like it just asks you to build/upgrade/put a bounty and whatever you can click while it plays itself.. It'd be nice if we could provide structured quests to parties giving us an active role in development and a layer of strategy/planning (balancing bringing in materials for the town, leveling heroes and keeping dangerous monsters at bay). If we had more management of our town it'd be nice to specialize and tailor production to the types of heroes and environment. The game desperately needs focus even if that means segmenting actions (having a town management set up phase/let the day play out + questing phase) This is a game that lacks focus, but I hope receives iteration on it's concept. I don't think post launch support of this game will drastically improve the game. I got this 40% off and unfortunately feel like I paid too much.

I REALLY want to be able recommend this game, it does SO much really well. The art style is really fun and the animations are great. Unit prestige and constructing your city are super fun, and the perks add a little flare that I find very enjoyable. Unfortunately, my main issue with the game is kind of the whole gimmick of the game, the quest giving system. The UI around it is clunky, unit response is too slow and they get distracted too easily. I will assign a defend quest to a farm and the units will get distracted by some enemies that are in the way and by the time they finish their fight the farm is either destroyed or I need to send them somewhere else. It's tedious, and I've spent far too much of my limited playtime watching my castle get attacked while my units are super far away and I don't have enough money to entice them to move quicker. I feel like this game would be far better with a classic unit control scheme for the overworld, click and drag to select units, right click to send them somewhere. When having units brave the dungeons, maybe that could be where gold plays a part, depending on the personality of the unit they may require more or less gold to explore, or something similar to that. The tutorial is very underbaked, and because of that certain systems I really did not understand (Still not sure what the blacksmith does), compound that with text that I find very hard to read (I'm on 1080p and the text is small and seems to lack aliasing) and the learning experience is quite difficult. All that being said I hope the potential of this game gets fully realized, and I hope my criticism is constructive. I am eagerly waiting for the issues to be solved, and will absolutely be checking patch notes to see what they fix. But right now, I cannot recommend this game due to its core some being strong enough.

One of the better Majesty-like games to come out in recent years. The artstyle, music and general asthetic are all quite nice (if you enjoy anime-esque stuff obviously) and it does more than try and be a straight up clone of majesty. It has a roguelite aspect as you unlock buildings and passives through randomized rewards at the start of a mission and by completing challenges throughout a mission. Some buildings have adjacency bonuses that give them bonuses when next to other buildings. There are some areas where it can improve though. You start off with at least 2 unit producing buildings at the start of a mission but getting more than that seems completely random. There are also some units which are just straight up better than other similar types so if you just get bad luck and only get 2 meh unit buildings to start with and no others throughout a mission it can be extremely difficult to do well. Also, there is no description of what abilities a unit actually has so you kind of have to learn through trial and error. This is a weird choice as units have a character screen showing their stats and even their inventory so not showing what their abilities do is strange. There is also the issue of difficulty. On the campaign type map where you pick missions and each one have a star rating, the difficulty can vary widely, and the higher start missions can sometimes just feel impossible as you get swarmed by higher level enemies and you just don't have the heroes to deal with them. The game definitely needs some more adjustments and a few quality of life updates but overall there is more good here than bad so I give this an upvote. I picked it up on sale during early access so it is good bang for buck for the price I paid. I just hope to see more improvements in the future.

Many of the issues I notice people talking about in their reviews are things that you learn, as you play. I'll explain some of the core features down below. Note that I ended up jumping in without doing the tutorial and did end up losing 2-3 times before I finally got the hang of things, this can take a few hours of gameplay, depending on the objectives you need to complete in order to win. Some of the objectives are to last a specific number of days, some are to defeat a specific boss and some are to beat a specific enemy building(s) it will tell you when you select the tile. Days are calculated by waves of enemies that are sent to you each night, and cleared. You can see the progression towards the next wave at the top right of your screen, it'll slowly burn down as the day progresses. Enemies for these waves are sent out specifically from nearby dungeons, note that these can be explored for loot, to fight the dungeon boss or obtain legendary treasure - That's how you can identify them. You will need to send out quests in order for your characters to complete tasks, almost always pressing "Urgent" in the quest window will result in immediate interest to do the task, just make sure you have idle adventurers available to do the task. Terraforming is your friend, especially when city building and planning, you'll find that certain buildings pair together, (i.e. a Tavern and any Unit creation building) You can use terraforming to get rid of pesky lakes, ravines or similar as well, it's a very useful tool. If you want advice on a specific unit to focus because you're struggling to clear levels, I find that the Mooladin is great because she has a built-in heal and becomes substantially stronger as she levels. Other units without a heal or sustain, tend to struggle quite a bit. Note that on every tile that you start, you have 3 perks that you can choose immediately, selected by clicking the perk button at the top left. This is important because perks are needed to unlock unit creation buildings and powerful buffs. For those looking to buy: Pros: - Music with a lot of heart and soul - Cute graphics and funny shenanigans that often keep things light and fun - Varying degrees of difficulty based on how you choose your map tiles (difficulty shown by amount of skulls) - If you like city builders + RTS or games like Rimworld, you'll probably like this game Cons: - Punishing towards new players - Tutorial is difficult to follow(?) (I can't confirm this, as I skipped the tutorial) - Sometimes the abilities or attack AI can miss, even when it looks like a clean hit - Slightly unbalanced unit types (See unit suggestion in my guide for a well-rounded unit) I hope this review helped some of you. It's a shame to see such an awesome game with mixed reviews. Maybe the tutorial isn't great and could be improved, though I'm unsure because I skipped it (like I do in 95% of games I play) Either way, the game is a bit of a learning curve, but when you get the hang of it, it can be quite a lot of fun! TDLR; The above is mostly a guide, explaining how to play. Otherwise, expect to put in a few hours to learn how to play, you'll fail a couple times but that's part of the learning process.
